name: Peak Charles National Park
reason: Rule 1 met on re-look: Parks WA (DBCA) visitor page describes the granite peak visible 50 km away, walks on Peak Charles and Peak Eleanora, orchids, birds and a campground; rule 2: free, open access, a half-day walk.
objection: Only one counted source; 4WD/gravel access and the summit is for advanced walkers only, so most visitors walk the base slopes.

name: Frank Hann National Park
reason: Rule 1: Parks WA visitor page (wildflowers along Lake King-Norseman Road, bushwalks); open and free.
objection: No facilities or marked walks; the page itself says you can see it from your car on a through road, so it may be a drive-through rather than a place to stop for half an hour. One source.

name: Matuwa Kurrara Kurrara National Park
reason: Rules 1 and 2 fail: no visitor page (the Parks WA URL is a 404) and the only reports (ExplorOz, 2024 forum) say traditional owners are not yet receiving visitors; camping and tourism not permitted.
objection: A new (2023) national park; if DBCA opens visitor access it should be reconsidered.

name: Credo Conservation Park
reason: Rule 1: Parks WA visitor page (bush walks, campground, salmon gum woodland, ghost-town relics, Rowles Lagoon, shearing shed); rule 2: open to the public.
objection: One counted source for a marginal place; the page warns of active mining leases and unsecured shafts, and permission is needed for some sites.

name: Burra Rock Conservation Park
reason: Two counted sources: Parks WA visitor page and Wikivoyage Coolgardie (See: the woodline dam and granite-slab catchment wall); picnic, camping, relics: rule 2 met.
objection: A picnic stop with a dam and rusted machinery; a modest draw outside the local area.

name: Gathercole Nature Reserve
reason: Two counted sources: Parks WA page (2.2-3.1 km loop trail over a granite outcrop, spring wildflowers, views) and the Wongan Hills board page; a walk of an hour satisfies rule 2.
objection: Mainly a spring wildflower draw; out of season it is a small local reserve walk.

name: Boyagin Nature Reserve
reason: Rule 1: Parks WA visitor page; rule 2: bushwalks, climb Boyagin Rock (50 m) for views, picnic, numbats and tammar wallabies. Kept as one spot with Boyagin Rock (same place, same point).
objection: One counted source; Parks WA's own quoted review says the rock is a long walk from the car park. Merge with the Boyagin Rock candidate.

name: Mount Magnet Mining and Pastoral Museum
reason: Rule 1: Australia's Golden Outback board page listing (Mount Magnet) names its collection of mining and farming relics and photographs; rule 2: an indoor visit.
objection: One source; a small volunteer-run town museum whose hours are unconfirmed; only if passing through.

name: Mount Magnet Tourist Trail
reason: Rule 1: Australia's Golden Outback board page names the 37 km trail through old and new mine sites to Warrmboo Hill views, a granite amphitheatre and a cave.
objection: It is a self-drive route rather than one place (rule: a spot is a place); the spot may better be Warrmboo Hill or the granite formations it visits. One source.

name: The Granites
reason: Rule 1: Australia's Golden Outback board page listing: a significant Aboriginal rock art site 7 km north of Mount Magnet; rule 2: open granite outcrop to explore.
objection: One counted source for a marginal place; cultural-sensitivity and access conditions are unconfirmed.

name: Lennonville
reason: Rule 1: Australia's Golden Outback board page (Mount Magnet) names exploring the remains of abandoned settlements such as Lennonville.
objection: Named in passing only; little is left of the townsite, so it may not hold a visitor for half an hour (rule 2). One source.

name: Cue Heritage Discovery Centre
reason: Rule 1: Australia's Golden Outback board page listing (Cue): displays from pre-settlement to mining with a giant map; rule 2: indoor visit.
objection: One source; a small interpretive display, likely under half an hour, and possibly the same building as the Cue visitor centre.

name: Big Bell Ghost Town
reason: Rule 1: Australia's Golden Outback board page listing (Cue): ghost town of the early-1900s Big Bell mine; open-access ruins.
objection: One source; ruins next to a mine lease, access conditions unconfirmed; a marginal stop.

name: Great Fingall Mine
reason: Rule 1: Australia's Golden Outback board page (Cue) names the Great Fingall Mine ruins and the old government buildings at Day Dawn.
objection: Named in a list only; the heritage mine office is largely viewed from outside (rule 2 exterior-only risk). One source.

name: Nallan Lake
reason: Rule 4 and rule 2 fail: the source recommends it only after heavy rain for a picnic, so it is not there whenever a visitor arrives; a local picnic spot.
objection: Named by the board; after rain it may be pleasant.

name: Milly Soak
reason: Rule 4 and rule 2 fail: recommended only after heavy rain for a picnic; a local spot with no stated thing to see otherwise.
objection: Named by the board alongside Nallan Lake.

name: Murchison GeoRegion Trail
reason: A spot is a place: this is a regional road-trip route through many sites (Walga Rock, The Granites etc.), each of which is its own candidate; not a distinct place (rule 3).
objection: Board pages promote it; its individual geosites may deserve spots.

name: Meeka Rangelands Discovery Trail
reason: Rule 1: Australia's Golden Outback board page (Meekatharra): 3 km interpretive trail on Aboriginal history, nature and rangelands; a walk satisfies rule 2.
objection: One source; a local town interpretive trail, marginal for a traveller from elsewhere.

name: Meeka Town Heritage Walk
reason: Rule 3: a town heritage walk past mostly exterior buildings, named in passing; not a distinct place beyond the town itself.
objection: Board names it as a Meekatharra attraction.

name: Meekatharra Museum
reason: Rule 2: a photo and memorabilia display inside the shire office/library, well under half an hour; a library/civic building.
objection: Board gives it a listing with 100+ photographs.

name: Peace Gorge
reason: Rule 1: Australia's Golden Outback board page listing (Meekatharra): granite rock formations and picnic spot 5 km from town; open access.
objection: One source; a local picnic spot that may only hold a passing traveller.

name: Peak Hill
reason: Rule 1: Australia's Golden Outback board page (Meekatharra) names the ghost town's ruins and old gold mines; 2653 page views.
objection: Named in passing only; remote, beside a mining area, and what remains to see is unconfirmed. One source.

name: Nannine
reason: Rule 1: Australia's Golden Outback board page (Meekatharra) names the ghost town's ruins and old mines.
objection: Named in passing only; very little remains of the townsite; one source.

name: 25 Mile Well
reason: Rule 3: a restored roadside well kept as a tribute to drovers, a minor memorial and short pull-out on the highway.
objection: Board names it by name, which can lift a roadside stop.

name: Mulka's Cave
reason: Two counted sources: Wikivoyage Hyden (See: recess with about 450 handprints at The Humps) and the Australia's Golden Outback board page (Hyden & Wave Rock); rule 2: rock art plus The Humps walk trails.
objection: Part of The Humps reserve: if The Humps is also a candidate, keep them as one spot (Mulka's Cave and The Humps).

name: Lake Magic
reason: Two counted sources: Wikivoyage Hyden (pay at the resort kiosk and walk around the coloured gypsum lake) and the Australia's Golden Outback board page; rule 2 met.
objection: Sits beside a resort and is paid; best only at dawn and dusk; a short visit.

name: Gorge Rock
reason: Rule 1: Australia's Golden Outback board page listing: natural rock pool with panoramic farmland views near Corrigin.
objection: One source; a modest picnic stop.

name: The Lace Place
reason: Two counted sources: Wikivoyage Hyden (See: open daily 9-5, lace collection back to the 1600s) and the Australia's Golden Outback board page; rule 2: an indoor paid visit.
objection: A niche collection beside Wave Rock that few would make a trip for; friend test says only if at Wave Rock anyway.

name: Wave Rock Wildlife Park
reason: Two counted sources: Wikivoyage Hyden (See: daily 9-5, kangaroos, koalas) and the Australia's Golden Outback board page (wildlife park with koalas and white kangaroos).
objection: A small bush wildlife park, marginal beside Wave Rock itself.

name: Wattoning Historical Site
reason: Rule 1: Australia's Golden Outback board page listing: gnamma hole and two rock-lined wells from the 1800s.
objection: One source; a minor heritage site likely under half an hour (rule 3 minor-site risk).

name: Kokerbin Rock
reason: Counted sources: Central Wheatbelt Visitor Centre's Eastern Wheatbelt drive trail lists it under granite outcrops; the candidate also cites the Kellerberrin board page. Drive or walk to the summit, picnic area: rule 2.
objection: Its 'third-largest monolith' claim is disputed; a rural detour.

name: Kellerberrin Hill Lookout
reason: Rule 1: Australia's Golden Outback board page (Kellerberrin) names the walk or drive to the lookout for views.
objection: One source, named in passing; a local town lookout, short visit.

name: Kellerberrin Folk Museum
reason: Rule 1: Australia's Golden Outback board page (Kellerberrin) names the folk museum in the 1897 Agricultural Hall with Pioneer Park.
objection: One source; a small volunteer museum, hours unconfirmed.

name: Milligan Homestead
reason: Rule 2: 'keep an eye out for' a historic homestead along a road: seen from the road, no stated public access.
objection: Board names it.

name: Doodlakine Well
reason: Rule 3: a minor heritage well site on a walk trail, a short stop of local interest.
objection: Board names it as the reason Doodlakine existed.

name: Bandee Ski Lake
reason: Rule 4: water levels vary and the source says check before arriving; a local waterski lake, not reliably there.
objection: Board names it.

name: Merredin Peak Trail
reason: Two counted sources: Australia's Golden Outback board page listing (Golden Pipeline walk to the top of Merredin Peak, views) and Central Wheatbelt Visitor Centre's drive trail (Merredin Peak Reserve and Railway Dam); a walk: rule 2.
objection: A low town hill; mainly for those already in Merredin.

name: Merredin Water Tower
reason: Rule 3: the 1893 tower stands in the museum precinct and is part of the Merredin Railway Museum visit; on its own an exterior look.
objection: Board gives it a separate listing.

name: Merredin Military Museum
reason: Three counted sources: Wikivoyage Merredin (daily 10-3, adult $10), Australia's Golden Outback board page (WA's largest collection of restored military vehicles) and the Central Wheatbelt drive trail; rule 2.
objection: A regional collection, only a detour for those on the Great Eastern Highway.

name: Merredin Railway Museum
reason: Two counted sources: Wikivoyage Merredin (daily 11-2, $15) and the Australia's Golden Outback board page (restored station, signal tower, rolling stock); rule 2.
objection: Short opening hours; near-duplicate risk with the Military Museum precinct next door (separate museums, kept separately).

name: Merredin Heritage Walk
reason: Rule 3: a walk linking the Railway and Military museums and town buildings; its draws are those museums, not a distinct place.
objection: Board gives it a listing.

name: Collgar Wind Farm
reason: Rule 1: Australia's Golden Outback board page listing and the Merredin page suggest the drive to see the 111 turbines.
objection: Private energy infrastructure seen from the road; likely a short look, not half an hour (rule 2). One source.

name: Merredin CBH silo mural
reason: Rule 1: Australia's Golden Outback board page names the Kyle Hughes-Odgers silo artwork, and the Central Wheatbelt drive trail lists the PUBLIC Silo Trail; a quirky roadside icon travellers stop to photograph.
objection: A short photo stop; the silo trail as a whole may be listed elsewhere, making this part of a larger feature.

name: Cummins Theatre
reason: Rule 1: Wikivoyage Merredin and Australia's Golden Outback board page both name it; self-guided tours on weekdays and live shows.
objection: Interior access is weekdays only; otherwise an exterior heritage building (rule 2); a short visit.

name: Foxes Lair Nature Reserve
reason: Rule 1: Australia's Golden Outback board page (Narrogin): 60 ha bushland with 300 wildflower varieties and 40 bird species; walk trails.
objection: One source; a town-edge bushland reserve, close to the 'ordinary local reserve' negative.

name: Yilliminning Rock
reason: Rule 1: Australia's Golden Outback board page listing (Narrogin): granite rock with a walk, called a must-see.
objection: One source; a minor local outcrop.

name: Barna Mia Animal Sanctuary
reason: Two counted sources: Parks WA Dryandra page (Barna Mia Nocturnal Wildlife Experience, guided nocturnal tour to see bilbies, woylies, bandicoots) and Australia's Golden Outback board page (Narrogin); the sanctuary is the place.
objection: Visits are by booked guided tour only, and it sits inside Dryandra Woodland, so it could be treated as part of that larger spot.

name: Narrogin Old Court House Museum
reason: Rule 1: Australia's Golden Outback board page (Narrogin) names its memorabilia, photos and crafts.
objection: One source; a small local museum, hours unconfirmed.

name: Narrogin Arts and Mural Drive
reason: A spot is a place: a self-guided drive past scattered murals around town, not one place (rule 3).
objection: Board promotes it as a Narrogin attraction.

name: Wongan Hills Mount O'Brien Lookout
reason: Rule 1: Australia's Golden Outback board page (Wongan Hills): recently developed lookout with a panoramic view of the shire.
objection: One source; a local lookout. Name should drop 'Wongan Hills' (Mount O'Brien Lookout).

name: Mount Matilda Walk Trail
reason: Rule 1: Australia's Golden Outback board page listing: bushland walk trail to Mount Matilda 12 km from Wongan Hills.
objection: One source; a local walk, chiefly a spring wildflower draw.

name: Wongan Pioneer Museum
reason: Rule 1: Australia's Golden Outback board page listing: local history museum in the old hospital.
objection: One source; small local museum, hours unconfirmed.

name: Reynoldson's Flora Reserve
reason: Rule 1: Australia's Golden Outback board page listing: wildflower reserve near Wongan Hills (colour October to December).
objection: One source; outside the wildflower season it is an ordinary local reserve.

name: Boyagin Rock
reason: Duplicate of Boyagin Nature Reserve (same coordinates; the rock is the reserve's centrepiece): kept as one spot under the reserve.
objection: The rock is the draw; the merged spot could be named Boyagin Rock instead.

name: Bonnie Rock
reason: Rule 1: no counted source names the rock as a place to visit; the Wheatbelt Way names only the Bonnie Rock townsite, and the rest are campsite listings.
objection: Wheatbelt Way stop; may be worth a look in a recall pass.

name: Baladjie Rock
reason: Rule 1: Central Wheatbelt Visitor Centre's Eastern Wheatbelt drive trail lists it under granite outcrops; climb for views over Baladjie Lake.
objection: One counted source; remote picnic and camping spot.

name: Beringbooding Rock
reason: Rule 1: Wheatbelt Way (the regional trail's site) describes the rock, free camping, Australia's largest rock catchment tank and Kangaroo Soak; also in the Wheatbelt Way guidebook. Rule 2 met.
objection: Remote (70 km north of Mukinbudin on gravel); the Wheatbelt Way page is a blog post on the trail's site.

name: Datjoin Rock
reason: Rule 1: named as a Wheatbelt Way stop near Beacon with a picnic area (guidebook, not directly read).
objection: Source thin and not opened directly; a minor outcrop.

name: Elachbutting Rock
reason: Two counted sources: Wheatbelt Way (Monty's Pass cave, a rock wave, free camping) and the Central Wheatbelt Visitor Centre drive trail; rule 2 met.
objection: Remote, 100 km north of Westonia on gravel.

name: Jilakin Rock
reason: Rule 1: Tourism Western Australia's Kulin page: summit views over salt lakes, picnic spots, an isolated jarrah stand; rule 2 met.
objection: A detour stop, a single source; the Kulin Bush Races there are an event, not the reason to keep.

name: Puntapin Rock
reason: Rule 1: no counted visitor source found (Wikipedia only; Wikivoyage has no Wagin page).
objection: A gnamma-hole granite dome near Wagin; the shire may promote it.
